newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Bucaram says he'd rather die than resign.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Bucaram says he'd rather die than resign.

text.p: Ecuador's eccentric leader Abdala Bucaram -- signalling what may be a long fight to remove him from the presidency -- said on Saturday that he would rather die than step down in disgrace.
"They want to get me out of the presidency. (But) I swear on my children, on my family and on my country that I'd rather die than resign," he said.

The defiant remark by Bucaram, who was voted out of office by Congress on grounds of mental incompetency on Thursday, came in a speech to supporters in a working-class district on the outskirts of this Pacific coast city.
The city, Ecuador's largest, is Bucaram's home and the political power base from which he launched his populist candidacy for the presidency in April 1996.
In his speech, in which he identified himself as "the commander-in-chief of the poor," Bucaram also vowed to see out his full term of office, which ends in August 2000.

Surprisingly, given intense political pressure for his removal from the presidential palace in Quito, Bucaram also announced for the first time that he was planning to run for re-election sometime after 2000.
Ecuador's constitution bars anyone from serving two consecutive terms as president.
